lead.event: Bank Indonesia holds its BI Rate and cuts reserve requirements in its October policy package
lead.headline: Bank Indonesia holds BI Rate at 5.75% and cuts reserve requirements
lead.blurb: Conventional banks’ reserve requirement will fall from 9% to 8% on 1 November and 7% on 1 December. For Islamic banks and business units, it will drop from 7.5% to 6.5% and then 5.5% on those dates. At its 20–21 October meeting, BI raised the Deposit Facility rate to 5.00% and kept the Lending Facility at 6.50%. BI said a 2% reserve requirement cut could add around Rp190 trillion in liquidity.

macro_flows.event: MSCI’s Indonesia reclassification proposal prompts market-risk warnings and official responses
macro_flows.headline: MSCI’s Indonesia proposal prompts warnings of up to US$5.6 billion in outflows
macro_flows.blurb: MSCI proposes moving Indonesia from emerging to standalone status, with its classification unchanged during consultation through 30 April 2027. Goldman Sachs estimates passive outflows of up to US$5.6 billion. Airlangga Hartarto said assessment does not depend on one rating agency. A final decision is expected by 30 June 2027.

market_structure_policy.event: IDX sets quarterly reviews and November exclusions for high-concentration stocks
market_structure_policy.headline: IDX sets quarterly reviews and November exclusions for 80 high-concentration stocks
market_structure_policy.blurb: HSC stocks account for about 18% of the IHSG. After meeting with MSCI on 19 October, BEI said it will review them every three months, allowing stocks that no longer meet the criteria to return to the IHSG. They are also barred from IDX80, IDX30 and LQ45.
market_structure_policy.copy_decision: rewritten: moved from lead to story

market_structure_policy.event: IDX suspends trading in MSIN and BSWD
market_structure_policy.headline: IDX suspends MSIN and BSWD after BSWD gains 438.33%
market_structure_policy.blurb: The temporary suspensions took effect in the regular and cash markets on 21 October as a cooling-down measure and to protect investors. MNC Digital Entertainment fell 31.21% to 119 in one week, while Bank of India Indonesia, whose shares have high ownership concentration, rose to 8,075 per share; BEI urged market participants to heed company disclosures.

market_structure_policy.event: OJK considers further sanctions in DSSA, BREN and CUAN trading cases
market_structure_policy.headline: OJK weighs further sanctions in DSSA, BREN and CUAN cases after Rp2.1 trillion fines
market_structure_policy.blurb: OJK also said the three cases will face criminal enforcement. Fines totaled Rp1.5 trillion in the Dian Swastika Sentosa case, Rp500 billion in Barito Renewables Energy’s and Rp100 billion in Petrindo Jaya Kreasi’s, following evidence of market manipulation and concealed order identities. OJK may impose further sanctions on violators, not the listed companies, after establishing legal grounds.
market_structure_policy.copy_decision: rewritten: regrouped, 1 of its articles moved out

capital_raising_buybacks.event: EMAS plans a private placement of up to 1.47 billion shares
capital_raising_buybacks.headline: EMAS plans private placement of up to 1.47 billion shares
capital_raising_buybacks.blurb: Merdeka Gold Resources’ controlling shareholder’s stake would fall from 64.83% to 58.94% if all shares are issued, with control unchanged. The placement could raise US$559.05 million, but no investors had expressed interest. Independent shareholders vote on the plan on 26 November.
capital_raising_buybacks.copy_decision: rewritten: 1 new articles with a new fact: If fully issued, the controlling shareholder’s stake falls from 64.83% to 58.94%, without a change in control.

capital_raising_buybacks.event: TINS secures a DHE-SDA facility from Bank Mandiri
capital_raising_buybacks.headline: TINS signs up to Rp4 trillion DHE-SDA facility with Bank Mandiri
capital_raising_buybacks.blurb: Timah will use the standby credit line for working capital and liquidity management. The revolving limit is valid for 12 months from signing, while non-revolving drawdowns have tenors of three to 12 months and require blocking DHE-SDA or other funds. Management said the transaction will not affect operations, financial condition or business continuity.

capital_raising_buybacks.event: CENT secures loan facilities for refinancing
capital_raising_buybacks.headline: CENT secures Rp12.48 trillion in loan facilities for refinancing
capital_raising_buybacks.blurb: Centratama and subsidiaries signed the agreements on 19 October with 14 creditors, including DBS Bank and MUFG Bank. The facilities will mainly refinance existing loans, cover fees and expenses, and settle hedge-counterparty obligations. Two shareholder loan maturities were extended to 31 December 2031.

capital_raising_buybacks.event: BCA extends its share buyback period through October 23
capital_raising_buybacks.headline: BCA extends share buyback through 23 October
capital_raising_buybacks.blurb: BCA’s buyback, initially scheduled to run through 21 October, now runs from 19–23 October. It has a maximum fund of Rp5 trillion under a 12-month program approved on 12 March, which runs through 11 March 2027.
capital_raising_buybacks.copy_decision: rewritten: moved from flash to story

earnings_guidance.event: PPRE reports a nine-month net loss
earnings_guidance.headline: PPRE reports a Rp161.61 billion nine-month net loss
earnings_guidance.blurb: PP Presisi swung from a Rp104.97 billion profit in January-September 2025 as revenue rose 19.86% to Rp3.32 trillion. Cost of revenue climbed 34.25% to Rp2.94 trillion, while gross profit fell 33.03% to Rp387.06 billion.

earnings_guidance.headline: PGEO targets 1.8 GW of installed capacity by 2034
earnings_guidance.blurb: Pertamina Geothermal Energy aims to reach 1 GW by 2028, up from 727 MW currently, with estimated investment of US$5.36 billion to US$6.43 billion. It plans to use internal capital, remaining IPO proceeds and green financing, alongside a joint venture with PLN; Lumut Balai Unit 3 is slated to start commercial operations in 2029.

earnings_guidance.event: Samuel Sekuritas assigns TINS a Buy rating
earnings_guidance.headline: Samuel Sekuritas gives TINS a Buy rating with a Rp5,000 target price
earnings_guidance.blurb: Managing Director Harry Su cited tight global tin supply and positive prospects, with a 5,720-ton market deficit in 1H26. Timah posted Rp2.71 trillion in first-half net profit, above its initial full-year target of Rp1.61 trillion. Risks include a tin price correction, weaker electronics demand, and the need to raise production and control costs.

deals_control.event: CIMB Group explores BNGA privatization or delisting over free-float rules
deals_control.headline: CIMB Group weighs BNGA privatization or delisting as float stands at 7.5%
deals_control.blurb: CIMB Niaga is assessing a go-private deal that CIMB Group estimates would cost around Rp3.3 trillion, based on 1.86 billion public shares at Rp1,550 each. No final decision has been made, with minimum free-float rules set to rise to 12.5% by March 2027 and 15% by March 2028.

deals_control.event: SILO completes the first-stage acquisition of three companies
deals_control.headline: SILO completes first-stage acquisition of three companies for Rp828.67 billion
deals_control.blurb: Siloam and subsidiary Megapratama Karya Bersama completed the purchase of Buton Bangun Cipta, Menara Abadi Megah and Nusa Bahana Niaga. Analysts see potential long-term gains in hospital asset ownership and rental efficiency, but say higher interest and depreciation expenses could weigh on near-term profit.
